stages.alt: NIFTY 50 daily candles through 2 September 2016. The prior upper zone is highlighted; subsequent candles are hidden.
stages.title: Stage 1 · Before the break
stages.prompt: What makes this a plausible prior upper area, and what would count as a break on this daily chart?
stages.placeholder: Name the prior evidence, your breakout convention, and one thing that would remain uncertain.

stages.alt: The same NIFTY 50 chart through 8 September 2016, now showing several closes above the highlighted zone.
stages.title: Stage 2 · The move closes outside
stages.prompt: Price has now closed above the zone for several sessions. What is better supported now—and what is still not guaranteed?
stages.placeholder: State your revised view, the evidence for it, and a specific condition that would weaken it.

stages.alt: The complete teaching window through 16 September 2016, showing price later returning below the original zone.
stages.title: Stage 3 · Later evidence
stages.prompt: How should you revise your earlier view now that price has moved back below the original zone?
stages.placeholder: Explain which earlier evidence still mattered, what changed, and what you would avoid claiming in hindsight.

quiz.q: A wick crosses above resistance but the candle closes back inside the zone. What is the most precise description?
options: The breakout is confirmed.
Price penetrated the area intraday but did not close beyond the chosen boundary.
The level has become support.
quiz.feedback: The high records an excursion; the close records where the session finished. They are not identical observations.

quiz.q: Two closes beyond a zone guarantee continuation.
options: True
False
quiz.feedback: A time filter is a convention, not a guarantee. The historical example later closes back below its zone.

quiz.q: No volume surge appears on the chart. Does that alone prove the breakout is false?
options: Yes, volume is mandatory in every market.
No. Volume is one possible contextual input; assess the price sequence and chart context too.
Yes, unless the next candle gaps.
quiz.feedback: Practitioners differ on how volume should be used. The course should not turn it into a universal pass/fail rule.

quiz.q: A fixed 20-point buffer means the same thing on every instrument and volatility regime.
options: True; points always have the same significance.
False; its meaning depends on instrument scale and current movement.
True, if the zone is drawn horizontally.
quiz.feedback: Fixed-distance, percentage and volatility-scaled conventions have different trade-offs. None is universal.

quiz.q: After two closes beyond the zone, price later returns inside it. What is the best review?
options: The earlier closes were not real observations.
The rule was consistent, but later evidence weakened the continuation interpretation.
A short trade is automatically required.
quiz.feedback: Later evidence changes the current interpretation; it does not erase what was observable at the earlier stage.

stages.alt: NIFTY 50 daily candles through 14 August 2014, with the candidate former-resistance zone highlighted.
stages.title: Stage 1 · The old upper area
stages.prompt: Which visible reactions support this candidate band, and what alternative boundary could another careful analyst defend?
stages.placeholder: Record the reactions you rely on and what your band excludes.

stages.alt: The same chart through 22 August 2014, showing the break and a later candle whose low approaches the zone edge.
stages.title: Stage 2 · The return approaches
stages.prompt: Did price enter the chosen band, touch its edge or just approach it? What does the close add?
stages.placeholder: Describe the low and close relative to the zone; do not call the outcome confirmed yet.

stages.alt: The full selected NIFTY 50 window through 18 September 2014, with later price remaining above the candidate area.
stages.title: Stage 3 · Later evidence
stages.prompt: What does the later sequence support, and what claim would go beyond the evidence?
stages.placeholder: Explain how your interpretation changed and what remains unproven.

quiz.q: Does every breakout need to return to its origin?
options: Yes, a retest is required.
No. Price may continue without returning.
Only if the first candle closes outside the zone.
quiz.feedback: A retest can offer additional evidence, but it is not mandatory.

quiz.q: Former resistance definitely becomes support after price returns from above.
options: True
False
quiz.feedback: Role reversal is a hypothesis; price can hold, cross through or remain ambiguous.

quiz.q: What should you do if the zone seems to need a new boundary after later candles appear?
options: Move it silently to fit the outcome.
Record the revision and the new evidence that justified it.
Pretend the original boundary always included the new candles.
quiz.feedback: Revising a zone is possible, but the revision should be explicit to avoid hindsight-fitting.

quiz.q: A return touches the band but the sequence then closes repeatedly inside the old range. What is the safest description?
options: The retest succeeded because it touched the band.
The role-reversal hypothesis is weakened by the later closes inside the prior range.
The next move must reach the opposite range edge.
quiz.feedback: Touching the area is not enough to determine the response; the later closes matter.

quiz.q: A move continues without a return to the original zone. What does that establish?
options: The breakout was invalid.
Only that the return did not happen in this window; it is not a required step.
You must chase the move.
quiz.feedback: The market does not owe a retest. Missing one is not evidence that every breakout is invalid.

stages.alt: NIFTY 50 daily candles through 19 January 2018, showing the candidate former-resistance band before the breakout.
stages.title: Stage 1 · Before the breakout attempt
stages.prompt: Which visible reactions define your candidate area? What would count as contradictory evidence later?
stages.placeholder: State the initial hypothesis, prior evidence, and a specific invalidation condition.

stages.alt: The same NIFTY 50 chart through 1 February 2018, showing a move above the band and a return that still closes above it.
stages.title: Stage 2 · The return looks acceptable
stages.prompt: At this point, what interpretation is plausible? What evidence is still missing?
stages.placeholder: Write the provisional view before you see the next sessions.

stages.alt: The same NIFTY 50 series through 20 February 2018, showing the close below the band and later weakness.
stages.title: Stage 3 · The thesis is challenged
stages.prompt: Which specific new evidence weakens the continuation thesis? Does it guarantee an opposite trade?
stages.placeholder: Record the contradiction, your revised view, and what remains uncertain.

quiz.q: Price breaks above a zone and later closes back inside the prior range. What is the most careful conclusion?
options: The next move must be lower.
The return is contradictory evidence against sustained continuation; assess the later sequence.
The original area was drawn incorrectly.
quiz.feedback: The failure weakens the original thesis. It does not guarantee direction or prove that the original zone was invalid.

quiz.q: What distinguishes a failure test from a single wick beyond a zone?
options: Any wick is enough to prove the failure test.
The sequence includes a move beyond a prior pivot or area and a quick reversal that challenges the initial move.
A volume surge is mandatory.
quiz.feedback: The sequence and the response matter. One wick beyond a boundary does not establish the complete pattern.

quiz.q: Price fails to hold beyond resistance, then later reclaims the original boundary and remains above it. What should you record?
options: The first failure never happened.
The reclaim is new evidence that may weaken the failure interpretation; preserve both events.
The original continuation thesis is guaranteed to succeed now.
quiz.feedback: The sequence changes as new candles appear. A reclaim challenges the current label without erasing earlier observations.

quiz.q: Does high volume on a failed breakout prove stop hunting?
options: Yes; high volume proves that stops were triggered intentionally.
No. Volume describes activity in the feed; it does not prove hidden motive.
Only if the candle closes outside the zone.
quiz.feedback: The data feed and its baseline matter, but OHLCV alone cannot establish who acted or why.

quiz.q: In a hypothetical failed-upside-break setup, what is a defensible structural reference for an initial stop?
options: A fixed line just above the old zone, regardless of the failure high.
Beyond the failure extreme that would undermine the failure thesis, with appropriate room; if that distance is too large, reduce exposure or pass.
Exactly one fixed tick amount on every instrument.
quiz.feedback: The structural reference is the extreme that would invalidate the failed-breakout interpretation. It is not a universal buffer, and stop orders may fill worse than the stop price during gaps or fast markets.
